digo_source: Mgombato ('kapu lemon', 'limau lemon'); Pakia ('Mlimau / Mkapu' shared by all Digo)

teaser.en: Digo has two words for the lemon, *limau* and *kapu*, and both are understood by Digo speakers everywhere.

summary.en: *Mlimau* or *mkapu* is the lemon tree, grown beside homesteads for its large yellow fruit. Its juice goes into drinks and into everyday cooking.

about.en: The lemon is a small citrus tree with glossy, pointed leaves and, often, a few sharp thorns on the twigs. Its white flowers are sweetly scented. The fruit is larger than a lime and ripens to bright yellow, with a sour, juicy flesh and an aromatic skin.

where.en: Lemon trees are kept close to the house, in homesteads and home gardens along the south coast, alongside limes and oranges.

uses.en: The juice is squeezed into drinks and used in cooking.

names.en: The tree is *mlimau* or *mkapu*, and the fruit *limau* or *kapu*. Both names are shared by all Digo speakers. Swahili uses *mlimau* for the tree and *limau* for the fruit. In English it is lemon.

reason.en: Same genus; the smaller, sourer lime

definition.en: A lemon; another Mgombato word alongside limau.

sources: Mwalonya, Nicolle, Nicolle & Zimbu, Mgombato: Digo-English-Swahili Dictionary (BTL / Digo Language and Literacy Project, 2004; e-version 2005)

Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
